take_homes: Access and use are different numbers. When someone reports licences rolled out, I ask how many people actually use them and for what.
A plan with unnamed owners is not a plan. I look for the name that answers for it.
Before buying, ask what the person does today and what would make them drop it. Test with one person before spending more.

monday.move: Ask the controller and one other finance person how they do month-end variance commentary today, and what would make them change. Look at our existing unused licences before any new one.
monday.who: The controller, plus whoever owns our licence list
monday.stop_condition: If neither would change what they do today, I drop it and ask for no budget.
monday.blocker: IT has not approved the tool for finance data.

misconception.why: I still read this as licence buying. But the point that access and absorption are different, and that I keep paying for unused licences, makes me think the capability sits in the people. I am not convinced yet. I never saw the agent work.

one_line: The lecture hit my licence problem, but the exercises assume you already have an agent and a memory folder. I didn't, and there was no figure anywhere.
